prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory whose main language got its first Pearl of Great Price between 1955 and 1979
prompts.text_original: A country or territory whose main local language got its first Pearl of Great Price (selections or full) between 1955 and 1979
prompts.citation: Church translations table, Pearl of Great Price; Global Histories chronologies: Japan, Tonga, Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan, Thailand
prompts.note: France, Switzerland and Belgium are out (French selections from 1908), and so is Norway (Norwegian selections from 1934).
prompts.summary: After 1950 the Pearl of Great Price spread into many new languages, often bound with the Doctrine and Covenants. Finnish and Japanese came in the mid-1950s, Tongan in 1959, Italian in 1965, Korean in 1968, Chinese and Samoan in 1976, Tahitian in 1978, and Indonesian and Thai in 1979.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: The Japanese Pearl of Great Price came out in Tokyo in 1955 with the Doctrine and Covenants (the translations table says 1957).

answers.name: South Korea
answers.fact: The first Korean Pearl of Great Price was published in 1968.

answers.name: China
answers.fact: Chinese, its main language, got its first Pearl of Great Price in April 1976, published in Hong Kong.

answers.name: Finland
answers.fact: The first Finnish Pearl of Great Price was published in 1955.

answers.name: Hong Kong
answers.fact: The Chinese Pearl of Great Price was published in Hong Kong in April 1976.

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: The translations table dates the first Italian Pearl of Great Price to 1965.

answers.name: Tonga
answers.fact: The Tongan edition is dated 1959; the first 500 copies reached Nuku'alofa on 17 March 1960.

answers.name: Taiwan
answers.fact: The Chinese Pearl of Great Price reached Taipei in April 1976.

answers.name: Samoa
answers.fact: The Samoan Pearl of Great Price was published in 1976.

answers.name: American Samoa
answers.fact: Samoan is its main language; the Samoan Pearl of Great Price came out in 1976.

answers.name: Indonesia
answers.fact: The Indonesian Pearl of Great Price was published in 1979.

answers.name: Macau
answers.fact: Macau's chronology records the Chinese Pearl of Great Price of April 1976, printed in Hong Kong.

answers.name: French Polynesia
answers.fact: The Tahitian Pearl of Great Price was published in 1978.

answers.name: Thailand
answers.fact: Thai translations of the Doctrine and Covenants and Pearl of Great Price were published in 1979.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a people judged in Zephaniah 2: Philistines, Moab, Ammon, Assyria, or the Nile land of Cush
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a people judged in Zephaniah 2 (Philistines, Moab, Ammon, the Ethiopians of Cush on the Nile, Assyria)
prompts.summary: Zephaniah 2 calls Judah to seek meekness, then names the peoples who will be judged: the Philistine cities of Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod and Ekron, Moab and Ammon, the Ethiopians, and Assyria with its capital Nineveh. The Bible's Ethiopia, or Cush, was the Nile land south of Egypt, today Sudan, not modern Ethiopia.

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: The Lord will destroy Assyria and make Nineveh a desolation (Zephaniah 2:13).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Ashkelon, Ashdod and Ekron were Philistine cities (Zephaniah 2:4).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Moab and the children of Ammon shall be as Sodom (Zephaniah 2:8-9).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Gaza shall be forsaken (Zephaniah 2:4); it lies in the Gaza Strip.

answers.name: Sudan
answers.fact: Ye Ethiopians also, ye shall be slain (Zephaniah 2:12); Bible Ethiopia, or Cush, ran south from Syene along the Nile, today Sudan.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country whose youth joined West Africa's 2010 celebrations of the Book of Mormon's 180th anniversary
prompts.text_original: A country whose youth joined the August 2010 West Africa celebrations of the 180th anniversary of the coming forth of the Book of Mormon
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies: Liberia (Aug 2010), Benin (dated Aug 2011)
prompts.note: Liberia's chronology dates it August 2010; Benin's says August 2011. 1830 plus 180 is 2010.
prompts.summary: The Book of Mormon was first published in 1830. To mark 180 years, more than 11,000 young people in seven West African countries held celebrations: Liberia, Nigeria, Benin, Togo, Ghana, Cote d'Ivoire and Sierra Leone.
